fullText.simplified:
第十六章、城头的绝望

    姜维在吵闹声中醒来，发现宫里正在发生一场大战。
    交战的双方，一方是宫里钟会的守卫，一方是宫外的魏军。
    “宫外的魏军？他们怎么进来了？”姜维又惊又急。
    他拉住一个逃命的小兵，问：“怎么回事？发生什么了？”
    小兵慌张得几乎说不出话来：“你快逃……宫外的魏军……他们……他们冲进来了，救……救锁在宫里的将军们……”
    “什么！宫外的魏军怎么知道将领们被锁起来了？”姜维问。
    “我……我不知道，秋……秋建带他们冲……进来的……”
    “秋建？”姜维的心凉了，秋建是钟会的助手，是除了钟会和自己以外，唯一出了那个门的人。他骗了钟会，去宫外给魏军报了信，然后带着他们冲进宫来救被锁起来的将领们。
    不应该等的！不应该给那两个小时的！当时就应该杀了那些犹豫的将领，然后直接去宫外接管他们的军队！
    姜维的肚子又在疼了，头也跟着疼起来。他扶着头，咬牙喊道：“钟会在哪里？”
    小兵却早已连滚带爬地跑了，没有人回答他了。
    头疼和肚疼越来越厉害，他提着长刀，慢慢向皇宫深处走去。有魏军士兵高喊着“杀啊”向他冲过来，但都倒在了他的刀下，然后满地翻滚，痛苦大叫。有刀箭向他飞来，他再举刀把那些刀箭打了回去。
    忽然，他听到城头上传来一阵大笑，那是钟会的声音！
    姜维抬头望去，看到钟会拿着长刀正与人对打，他一边挥刀，一边像疯了一样大笑：“来啊！来啊！有本事杀了我啊！”
    “小心！”姜维大叫，但还是晚了，一阵箭雨向钟会飞了过去。
    来不及躲开，钟会倒下了，身上插满箭，从高高的城头上掉了下来。
    “钟会！”姜维绝望地大喊。
    一个将领看到了姜维：“那是姜维！蜀国的降将，就是他要钟会造反的，杀了他！”
    立刻，一阵箭雨又向姜维飞了过来。姜维举刀，箭雨被打落，但马上另一阵更大的箭雨又飞了过来，姜维再也没有力气了。他倒下了，像钟会一样，他的身上也插满了箭。
    他倒在地上，头和肚子都不疼了，血正不断地从身体里流出，但他感受不到痛苦。他无力地望着远处掉落在城下全身插满箭的钟会，心里一片空白。钟会死了，他的救国计策失败了，他没有机会再走第三步了——钟会造反成功，成为蜀国皇帝，他再杀钟会，让蜀国死而复生。
    没有机会了，现在，一切都结束了。
fullText.traditional:
第十六章、城頭的絕望

    姜維在吵鬧聲中醒來，發現宮裡正在發生一場大戰。
    交戰的雙方，一方是宮裡鍾會的守衛，一方是宮外的魏軍。
    “宮外的魏軍？他們怎麼進來了？”姜維又驚又急。
    他拉住一個逃命的小兵，問：“怎麼回事？發生什麼了？”
    小兵慌張得幾乎說不出話來：“你快逃……宮外的魏軍……他們……他們衝進來了，救……救鎖在宮裡的將軍們……”
    “什麼！宮外的魏軍怎麼知道將領們被鎖起來了？”姜維問。
    “我……我不知道，秋……秋建帶他們衝……進來的……”
    “秋建？”姜維的心涼了，秋建是鍾會的助手，是除了鍾會和自己以外，唯一出了那個門的人。他騙了鍾會，去宮外給魏軍報了信，然後帶著他們衝進宮來救被鎖起來的將領們。
    不應該等的！不應該給那兩個小時的！當時就應該殺了那些猶豫的將領，然後直接去宮外接管他們的軍隊！
    姜維的肚子又在疼了，頭也跟著疼起來。他扶著頭，咬牙喊道：“鍾會在哪裡？”
    小兵卻早已連滾帶爬地跑了，沒有人回答他了。
    頭疼和肚疼越來越厲害，他提著長刀，慢慢向皇宮深處走去。有魏軍士兵高喊著“殺啊”向他衝過來，但都倒在了他的刀下，然後滿地翻滾，痛苦大叫。有刀箭向他飛來，他再舉刀把那些刀箭打了回去。
    忽然，他聽到城頭上傳來一陣大笑，那是鍾會的聲音！
    姜維抬頭望去，看到鍾會拿著長刀正與人對打，他一邊揮刀，一邊像瘋了一樣大笑：“來啊！來啊！有本事殺了我啊！”
    “小心！”姜維大叫，但還是晚了，一陣箭雨向鍾會飛了過去。
    來不及躲開，鍾會倒下了，身上插滿箭，從高高的城頭上掉了下來。
    “鍾會！”姜維絕望地大喊。
    一個將領看到了姜維：“那是姜維！蜀國的降將，就是他要鍾會造反的，殺了他！”
    立刻，一陣箭雨又向姜維飛了過來。姜維舉刀，箭雨被打落，但馬上另一陣更大的箭雨又飛了過來，姜維再也沒有力氣了。他倒下了，像鍾會一樣，他的身上也插滿了箭。
    他倒在地上，頭和肚子都不疼了，血正不斷地從身體裡流出，但他感受不到痛苦。他無力地望著遠處掉落在城下全身插滿箭的鍾會，心裡一片空白。鍾會死了，他的救國計策失敗了，他沒有機會再走第三步了——鍾會造反成功，成為蜀國皇帝，他再殺鍾會，讓蜀國死而復生。
    沒有機會了，現在，一切都結束了。

sentences.english: He fell, just like Zhong Hui, his body also pierced with arrows.

sentences.simplified: 他倒在地上，头和肚子都不疼了，血正不断地从身体里流出，但他感受不到痛苦。
sentences.traditional: 他倒在地上，頭和肚子都不疼了，血正不斷地從身體裡流出，但他感受不到痛苦。
sentences.pinyin: tā dǎo zài dì shang tóu hé dù zi dōu bù téng le xiě zhèng bú duàn de cóng shēn tǐ lǐ liú chū dàn tā gǎn shòu bú dào tòng kǔ
sentences.english: He fell to the ground. His head and stomach no longer hurt. Blood was steadily flowing from his body, but he felt no pain.

sentences.simplified: 他无力地望着远处掉落在城下全身插满箭的钟会，心里一片空白。
sentences.traditional: 他無力地望著遠處掉落在城下全身插滿箭的鍾會，心裡一片空白。
sentences.pinyin: tā wú lì de wàng zhe yuǎn chù diào luò zài chéng xià quán shēn chā mǎn jiàn de zhōng huì xīn li yí piàn kòng bái
sentences.english: He looked helplessly at Zhong Hui, who had fallen below the city wall, his body pierced with arrows, and his mind went blank.

sentences.simplified: 钟会死了，他的救国计策失败了，
sentences.traditional: 鍾會死了，他的救國計策失敗了，
sentences.pinyin: zhōng huì sǐ le tā de jiù guó jì cè shī bài le
sentences.english: Zhong Hui was dead, and his plan to save the country had failed.

sentences.simplified: 他没有机会再走第三步了——钟会造反成功，成为蜀国皇帝，
sentences.traditional: 他沒有機會再走第三步了——鍾會造反成功，成為蜀國皇帝，
sentences.pinyin: tā méi yǒu jī huì zài zǒu dì sān bù le zhōng huì zào fǎn chéng gōng chéng wéi shǔ guó huáng dì
sentences.english: He no longer had the chance to take the third step—Zhong Hui succeeding in his rebellion and becoming the emperor of Shu.

sentences.simplified: 他再杀钟会，让蜀国死而复生。
sentences.traditional: 他再殺鍾會，讓蜀國死而復生。
sentences.pinyin: tā zài shā zhōng huì ràng shǔ guó sǐ ér fù shēng
sentences.english: He would then kill Zhong Hui, bringing Shu back to life.

sentences.simplified: 没有机会了，现在，一切都结束了。
sentences.traditional: 沒有機會了，現在，一切都結束了。
sentences.pinyin: méi yǒu jī huì le xiàn zài yí qiè dōu jié shù le
sentences.english: There was no chance now. Everything was over.

sentence_translations: Chapter 16: Despair on the City Wall
Jiang Wei woke up to the sound of commotion and discovered that a great battle was taking place in the palace.
The two sides in the battle were Zhong Hui’s guards inside the palace and the Wei army from outside the palace.
“The Wei army from outside the palace? How did they get in?” Jiang Wei was both shocked and anxious.
He grabbed a fleeing soldier and asked, “What’s going on? What happened?”
The soldier was so flustered that he could barely speak:
“You must escape … the Wei army outside … they … they’ve broken in, rescuing … rescuing the generals locked in the palace …”
“What? How did the Wei army from outside the palace know that the generals had been locked up?” Jiang Wei asked.
“I … I don’t know, Qiu … Qiu Jian led them … in …”
“Qiu Jian?” Jiang Wei felt a chill in his heart.
Qiu Jian was Zhong Hui’s assistant and the only person, besides Zhong Hui and himself, who had gone through that door.
He deceived Zhong Hui, went outside the palace to inform the Wei army, and then led them in to rescue the generals who had been locked up.
I shouldn’t have waited! I shouldn’t have given those two hours!
I should have killed those hesitant generals right then and there, and then directly taken over their troops outside the palace!
Jiang Wei’s stomach started to hurt again, and his head began to ache as well.
Holding his head, he gritted his teeth and shouted, “Where is Zhong Hui?”
But the soldier had already run away, trying frantically to escape, and no one answered him.
His headache and stomachache were getting worse and worse.
He gripped his long sword and slowly walked deeper into the palace.
Wei soldiers charged at him, shouting, “Kill!” but they all fell under his blade, rolling on the ground and crying out in pain.
Swords and arrows flew toward him, and he raised his sword to deflect them back.
Suddenly, he heard loud laughter coming from the top of the city wall—it was Zhong Hui’s voice!
Jiang Wei looked up and saw Zhong Hui wielding a long sword, engaged in a fight with someone.
As he swung his blade, he laughed like a madman: “Come on! Come on! Kill me if you can!”
“Watch out!” Jiang Wei shouted, but it was too late—a volley of arrows had already flown toward Zhong Hui.
Unable to dodge in time, Zhong Hui fell, his body pierced with arrows, and he plummeted from the high city wall.
“Zhong Hui!” Jiang Wei cried out in despair.
A general saw Jiang Wei: “That’s Jiang Wei! The surrendered general of Shu. He’s the one who wanted Zhong Hui to rebel. Kill him!”
Immediately, another volley of arrows flew toward Jiang Wei.
Jiang Wei raised his sword, deflecting the volley of arrows.
But soon, an even larger volley of arrows came flying toward him, and Jiang Wei no longer had the strength.
He fell, just like Zhong Hui, his body also pierced with arrows.
He fell to the ground. His head and stomach no longer hurt. Blood was steadily flowing from his body, but he felt no pain.
He looked helplessly at Zhong Hui, who had fallen below the city wall, his body pierced with arrows, and his mind went blank.
Zhong Hui was dead, and his plan to save the country had failed.
He no longer had the chance to take the third step—Zhong Hui succeeding in his rebellion and becoming the emperor of Shu.
He would then kill Zhong Hui, bringing Shu back to life.
There was no chance now. Everything was over.
